summary: Re-test of M4-S03 (before-save record-triggered Flow stamping EntitlementId, BusinessHoursId and Priority on Case) after the third build, which corrected F-38: the org's run-3 mock-deploy message ('The test point for elementApiName Start contains the incompatible parameter value $Record of type InputTriggeringRecordUpdated. Remove the parameter or change the recordTriggerType for the flow.') led the builder to remove the InputTriggeringRecordUpdated parameter from the FlowTest's Start test point, leaving InputTriggeringRecordInitial as the sole test input -- confirmed by direct inspection: the flowtest file contains exactly one InputTriggeringRecordInitial occurrence and zero InputTriggeringRecordUpdated occurrences. Every other declared output (flow, Flow.settings, package.xml, flow-governance-policy.yaml, no-account-fallback-note.md) is byte-identical to build 1 per the runner's own SHA-256 comparison recorded in envelopes/M4-S03/2026-09-12T08-40-00Z.json. Both always-on checks (xml parse, manifest consistency) and all three declared checkers (record-triggered-flow-patterns, flow-element-naming-conventions, flow-governance) exit 0, check-outputs reports ok with nothing missing/empty/malformed, and the one declared manual test remains a well-formed Given/When/Then naming observable outcomes, deferred to the milestone gate. Status moved built -> tested. This run's tests/M4-S03/results.json and summary.md were overwritten in place and supersede the build-2 test record (run 2026-09-12T08-33-09Z), which tested the flow while it still carried the (org-rejected) InputTriggeringRecordUpdated parameter.
confidence_rationale: Every declared acceptance test either ran to an observed exit code or was correctly classified as manual; both always-on checks completed; check-outputs was ok; no checker was missing and no command test needed the deny-list.

process_observations.observation: The three-run correction sequence for F-38 (add InputTriggeringRecordInitial in build 2, then remove the co-existing InputTriggeringRecordUpdated in build 3) is fully traceable in the run history and in artefacts/M4-S03/deploy-order.md section 0's three-run table: the settled rule, proven live in both directions by the two mock-deploy rejections, is that a Create-triggered FlowTest takes InputTriggeringRecordInitial only, while Update/CreateAndUpdate take both. Direct grep of the flowtest file this run confirms exactly one InputTriggeringRecordInitial and zero InputTriggeringRecordUpdated occurrences.

All three declared checkers reproduced the same verdicts as the prior two test runs (record-triggered-flow-patterns: No issues found; naming: 0 error(s), 4 warning(s); governance: 0 error(s), 2 advisory), which is exactly what an unchanged flow XML plus a corrected-but-still-parseable FlowTest should produce -- none of the three checkers inspects FlowTest parameters, so their stability across all three builds is expected rather than a coverage gap being missed by chance.

check_flow_element_naming_conventions.py still reports four W-FAULT-TARGET warnings because every fault path on this before-save flow reconverges on a Decision element instead of a LogFault_<Parent> target; deploy-order.md already records this as a library gap rather than a defect in this artefact. Advisory only, exit 0, unchanged across all three builds.

deploy-order.md still carries the derived CasePriority value mapping (Severity 1 -> High, Premier -> High, else Medium) as UNVERIFIED rather than answered by a clarification; unrelated to the F-38 fix and still unresolved by this run, since step-tester does not adjudicate Salesforce design questions. Carried forward to the milestone gate unchanged.
M4-S03 is tested again with zero failures after the third build, and one manual test remains deferred to the milestone gate.
